paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Uncle Dan came to the house. He is Dad's older brother, and he is a kind man. He usually wears a jacket, but today he wore a blue shirt. "I am free today, because it is Saturday," he said. He had a big bag of fresh mangoes. The mangoes smelled sweet. "Why did you bring so many?" asked Lily. "Because I know that you love mangoes," said Uncle Dan.

Lily put the mangoes in a bowl, and she covered it with a white towel. "Why do you cover them?" asked Uncle Dan. "Because insects like sweet fruit," said Lily. "That is a good idea," said Uncle Dan. Lily smiled. Tom came into the kitchen with a football. "I have a lesson with Coach Matt at ten o'clock," he said. "Can you come and watch?"

"Of course I can," said Uncle Dan. "I want to see you play, because you are a good player." Tom put some money in his pocket. "I will buy cold water after the lesson, because it is hot," he said. Dad gave Uncle Dan a wide hat and sunglasses. "Please wear them, because the sun is very strong on the field," said Dad. Uncle Dan laughed and put them on.

At the field, Coach Matt called the players to the middle. "We will drink water every fifteen minutes," he said. "It is a very hot day, and water keeps you healthy." Uncle Dan sat under a tree. He took off his hat. The team did a lot of exercise, and Tom ran fast. "Why did you run so fast?" asked Uncle Dan after the lesson. "Because I wanted to show you my best," said Tom.

Uncle Dan bought two bottles of cold water for Tom. "You keep your money, because I want to pay," he said. They went home, and Lily brought out the mangoes. Everybody ate the sweet fruit at the table. The family talked and laughed for a long time. "I came today because I wanted to see my family," said Uncle Dan. "A good Saturday needs mangoes and a good game," said Tom.
